item.title: Broken glass and rubbish at sport field in Walsingham Linear Open Space, 24th August
item.description:
I would like to report the poor and potentially dangerous condition of the asphalt basketball court. There is a lot of small broken glass on the court, which appears not to have been swept for a long time. Children use this area to play basketball, football and ride scooters, so the broken glass poses a serious risk of injury. There is also a significant amount of rubbish and paper under the fence and in the bushes around the site. Could you please arrange for the area to be cleaned and the broken glass and rubbish to be removed?
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Athelstan Way, St Paul's Cray, Greater London

item.title: Narrow road for cyclists AND HGVs, 24th August
item.description:
Leonard Street is already a very narrow one-way road, with a cycle lane on one side and an e-bike parking bay on the other. The road is also frequently used by HGVs and delivery vans, which can leave very little space for cyclists to pass safely. As a result, cyclists are sometimes forced onto the pavement to get around larger vehicles, creating additional risk for pedestrians. It would be worth reviewing whether this section of Leonard Street could be made cycle-only, or whether access for larger vehicles could be restricted. Other potential improvements could include: Restricting HGV access where alternative routes are available Adding clearer segregation between the cycle lane and vehicle traffic Reviewing whether the current one-way layout is suitable for the volume of cycle traffic The current layout feels too constrained for the mix of cyclists, pedestrians, parked e-bikes and larger delivery vehicles using the street.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 24, Leonard Street, Finsbury, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Unclear pavement markings for bikes and pedestrians, 24th August
item.description:
The road and pavement markings at the crossing between Featherstone Street and Leonard Street are unclear. Cyclists and pedestrians are required to share a narrow crossing space, but the lack of clear markings makes it difficult to understand how the space should be used. This is leading to overcrowding and potentially unsafe interactions between cyclists and pedestrians travelling in both directions. Clearer markings and separation would help make the crossing safer and easier to navigate.
